summary: Phase 15 — SQL snake_case CSV header support. The single-line change in royalty_utils.normalize_header() (replace underscores AND hyphens with spaces, collapse whitespace) correctly enables the EXISTING alias list to recognise SQL-export headers (bulan_laporan, pendapatan_bersih, nama_label, …) WITHOUT regressing the Believe space-separated headers. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_phase15_snake_case_headers.py with 33 tests covering header normalization, detect_columns mapping, parse_period (YYYY-MM-DD), parse_amount (dot-decimal), parse_csv_bytes + iter_csv_file against the real /tmp/sql_revenues.csv, Believe regression, and a full end-to-end direct-to-R2 upload (initiate → PUT to R2 → finalize). RESULT: 33/33 PASS. The real SQL CSV produced 10 total_lines / 10 matched / 0 unmatched on the live backend. Both named Believe regression tests (TestParseCsv::test_semicolon_autodetect_and_indonesian_headers, TestParseCsv::test_row_values) STILL PASS unchanged.
critical_code_review_comments: normalize_header() correctly handles snake_case, kebab-case, BOM, mixed underscores, and uppercase — confirmed by 13 parametrized cases.

detect_columns() maps every canonical field from the 23-column SQL header set: period (from bulan_laporan), label_name, artist_name, release_title, track_title, isrc, upc, quantity, revenue_eur, gross_revenue_eur, unit_price_eur, mechanical_cost_eur, client_share_rate, sales_type, release_type, currency, platform, country.
Extra non-canonical column 'release_catalog_nb' is silently ignored — catalog_ref alias resolves to None (no false positive), no crash.
parse_amount('0.000181577974000') → 0.000181577974 (US dot-decimal); regression test confirms '0,000181577974000' → 0.000181577974 (EU comma-decimal) still works.

End-to-end upload of /tmp/sql_revenues.csv via the direct-to-R2 flow: 10 total_lines, 10 matched_lines, 0 unmatched_lines — confirms snake_case parsing works at the production code path (_process_csv_import_bg → iter_csv_file → detect_columns → _match_line).

rca_of_the_issue: ROOT CAUSE OF THE ORIGINAL BUG (already fixed by E1): normalize_header() in /app/backend/royalty_utils.py only lowercased and stripped headers but did NOT convert underscores or hyphens to spaces. HEADER_ALIASES uses space-separated forms like 'bulan laporan' and 'pendapatan bersih', so SQL exports with 'bulan_laporan' / 'pendapatan_bersih' headers never matched any alias → all columns returned None → every row was unmatched. FIX (single line in royalty_utils.py L135-L136): `s = s.replace('_', ' ').replace('-', ' '); s = ' '.join(s.split())`. This lets one alias list cover Believe (Bulan Laporan), SQL exports (bulan_laporan), kebab-case (bulan-laporan), and any mixed/double-underscore variations. VERIFIED via 33 tests including a full E2E upload of the user's real /tmp/sql_revenues.csv → 10/10 matched, 0 unmatched. NO REGRESSION on the Believe format.
